transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Janelle Huang (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - Acme), Priya Shah (Lead ML Eng), Diego Ramos (Infra), Sara Kim (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC objectives comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment modes. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, security requirements, and next steps.

Topics:
- Success criteria: latency SLOs, quality regressions, cost per 1M tokens
- Workload sizing: concurrency, qps, average tokens/request, peak patterns
- Benchmarks: dataset, metrics (p50/p90/p99, throughput, cost), test harness
- Timeline: pilot windows and decision gate for production mode

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I know we have about 40 minutes, i'll kick off, i'm samir from redwood inference, ae on the account. janelle will do the technical scoping.
[00:08] Liam: thanks samir, yeah we just want to lay out what success looks like and whether we should go hosted or reserved or private for the pilot.
[00:12] Janelle: great; quick question, priya, can you confirm the current stack? you mentioned a mix of serverless api gateway in front of nodejs services and some on-prem batch jobs?
[00:20] Priya: yeah that's right. most of the interactive feature calls hit our node service in k8s on EKS, but we also have nightly batch reranks that run on-prem in a data center.
[00:29] Diego: infra note - we prefer not to send any PII off region for now; so data residency is important and we have a corporate KMS and VPC peering requirements.
[00:37] Samir: totally understood. we can scope a private deployment if needed or dedicated with VPC peering and customer-managed keys.
[00:44] Sara: and timeline wise we are aiming for a pilot in June, production decision by end of July if things look good.
[00:50] Janelle: ok let's enumerate the success criteria - this helps pick mode. from our side typical POC success items are: 1) meet latency SLOs (p90 < 300ms for the interactive path), 2) quality parity to current baseline (we'll do eval prompts), 3) cost/throughput estimates within your budget, 4) security checklist (SOC2, SSO, audit logs)
[01:12] Priya: that p90 300ms is aggressive; our existing small LLM op is about 280ms avg today, but with peaks it can go higher. we need to know if hosted will have consistent tail latency.
[01:24] Janelle: good point. hosted has predictable performance generally but for strict tail SLOs and high sustained qps dedicated is usually recommended. private on-prem gives you full control but requires more setup and longer lead time.
[01:36] Liam: can you give us ballpark numbers for throughput? our current numbers: 60 rps steady, 250 rps peak bursts for a minute or two, average tokens per request about 350, with some long prompts up to 2000 tokens.
[01:50] Diego: also note the batch rerank job is ~10k items per run, we would like to run on GPUs during off hours.
[01:56] Samir: ok that's helpful. based on that profile, rough starting guidance: hosted for pilot if you want fastest time-to-value, but we'd need to run a benchmark with your prompts. dedicated reserved capacity or dedicated pools would lower per-token cost and give more predictable p99s for sustained load. private would be recommended if you have strict data residency and corporate KMS or air-gap constraints - it will add about 4-6 weeks to set up depending on network approvals.
[02:20] Priya: what's the connector story for our EKS services? do you support private link or VPC peering?
[02:25] Janelle: yes - dedicated supports VPC peering and private link, and private deployment sits inside your VPC entirely. hosted can be accessed via public API but we offer customer-specific network configs for enterprise customers.
[02:35] Sara: cost is a big factor. can you share a simple cost model: hosted tokens vs dedicated reserved monthly?
[02:40] Samir: yep we'll send scenarios. quick mental model: hosted is pay-as-you-go, so for low volume it's cheapest. for sustained high qps, dedicated committed capacity often reduces unit cost by 30-60% depending on commit. private has similar or lower run cost but adds infra and ops fees. we'll put numbers in the pricing doc.
[02:58] Liam: benchmark plan - we want to validate latency, quality, and cost. what's required from our side?
[03:04] Janelle: ideally we need: (1) a representative set of ~500 prompts for interactive flows, (2) a sample of batch rerank inputs (on the smaller side) and (3) traffic profile (per-minute qps distribution and concurrency). with those we can run multi-phase tests: warmup/kv-cache tests, steady-state throughput, and burst tests to simulate peaks.
[03:26] Priya: can we also measure p50/p90/p99 and GPU utilization?
[03:30] Janelle: yes, the benchmark harness will capture latency percentiles, tokens/sec, GPU memory and util, and estimated cost per 1M tokens. we'll also run ablation - different quantization and model variants - to evaluate quality vs cost.
[03:42] Diego: about the rerank batch, can you support batched GPU jobs? we might want to schedule them into a dedicated pool overnight.
[03:48] Samir: yes, dedicated and private support scheduled batch jobs; hosted can also run them but you'd pay on demand. many customers use dedicated pools for predictable batch windows.
[03:55] Sara: security caveats - we need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS for keys, and audit logs for all API requests. is that all standard?
[04:03] Janelle: that's standard. we have SOC2 report, SAML/SSO options, tenant RBAC and audit logs. for KMS you can bring your own key in dedicated/private - hosted has a managed key option and BYOK in enterprise plans.
[04:16] Liam: ok what about data retention and log redaction? our legal team won't allow raw logs to be stored >30 days or include PII.
[04:23] Samir: we can configure retention and redaction policies; private gives you most control. we'll include the data handling docs.
[04:30] Priya: for the POC, what would success criteria look like specifically? we should define pass/fail metrics.
[04:36] Janelle: propose: - Latency: p90 < 350ms and p99 < 1s for interactive flows during steady-state and burst tests - Quality: automated eval on 500 prompts with no more than 3% decline vs baseline on our eval metric (we'll accept +/- tolerance) - Cost: projected cost per 1M tokens within X% of your target (we'll fill number after pricing) - Ops: ability to authenticate via SSO and have audit logs available within 48 hours of request
[05:01] Sara: can we set a decision gate after benchmarks? e.g., if latency/quality/cost pass then move to a 3-month pilot on dedicated?
[05:07] Samir: absolutely, typical flow is: week 0 setup, week 1-2 benchmarks, decision gate, then 1-3 month pilot on dedicated or private depending on outcome.
[05:15] Liam: what's the expected setup time for dedicated vs private?
[05:18] Janelle: dedicated: 1-2 weeks for capacity provisioning and VPC peering; private: 4-6 weeks usually, depends heavily on network approvals and on-prem infra. hosted: minutes to hours if you don't need VPC peering.
[05:29] Diego: network approvals at our company are slow; if private is chosen it will add delay. we might prefer dedicated with VPC peering to meet residency and KMS requirements.
[05:38] Priya: question about model variants - do you support quantized variants and automatic fallback?
[05:42] Samir: yes, the platform supports multiple model variants including int8 quantized builds; smart routing can fallback to cheaper variants if latency or cost thresholds are hit, but for quality sensitive flows we recommend pinning model versions during the POC.
[05:55] Sara: will you run benchmarks against our dataset or do you need sanitized examples? legal might want sanitized examples.
[05:59] Janelle: sanitized examples are fine - for latency and throughput we don't need real PII. for quality evals it's best to have representative prompts but anonymized.
[06:07] Liam: what tooling do you provide to reproduce our benchmarks and charts? we want reproducible results to share with execs.
[06:12] Janelle: we provide a benchmark harness repo - a small driver that sends requests according to traffic profile, captures percentiles, and outputs CSVs and dashboards. we'll give access to the harness and the metrics dashboard.
[06:22] Priya: about costs during benchmark - is there any free trial or credits?
[06:26] Samir: we'll give pilot credits for benchmarking and initial testing, we'll include that in the pricing note.
[06:31] Diego: scaling question - how do you handle prefix caching and KV cache? our interactive flows have a lot of repeated prefixes.
[06:36] Janelle: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching; during the warmup you'll see reduced token compute for repeated prefixes. that's part of the optimization we'll measure.
[06:44] Sara: ok let's align on the benchmark schedule. prefer week of 05/31 as suggested?
[06:48] Liam: yes week of 05/31 works for us, we can aim to hand over artifacts by 05/26.
[06:53] Samir: perfect. i'll send the pricing doc and SOC2 links by monday. janelle, you'll own the benchmark plan?
[06:58] Janelle: yes i'll own it and schedule the kickoff with your infra team.
[07:02] Priya: for success criteria, we'll sign off on the p90/p99 and quality threshold. if we fail one metric, is there a remediation window?
[07:09] Samir: typically we do one remediation iteration - adjust batch sizes, quantization, model variant, and rerun benchmarks. if still failing, we document gaps and recommend path forward, could be dedicated or private depending on root cause.
[07:19] Sara: any quick call-outs about legal/procurement? Diego?
[07:22] Diego: procurement will need standard msla and need to see data processing agreement; we'll run that in parallel but it takes time.
[07:27] Samir: noted; i'll loop in our legal ops in the follow-up.
[07:30] Liam: ok final recap?
[07:32] Samir: recap - Redwood to send: pricing scenarios, SOC2 and security docs, benchmark harness and list of artifacts needed. Customer to send: sample prompts (~500 anonymized), batch sample, traffic profile CSV by 2026-05-26. Schedule benchmark kickoff week of 2026-05-31. Decision gate after 2 weeks of benchmarks to decide dedicated vs private.
[07:52] Sara: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:55] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedcated"), timestamps approximate every 20-40 seconds. Some speaker labels merged in export.
